original_test_intent: Demonstrate that ERoT/Aps firmware protections reject each approved corrupted, signature-invalid and rollback-invalid image, never replace the previous active firmware, and still permit a normal OS boot after AC recovery.
original_method: On a dedicated recovery-ready SUT, map exact ERoT/Aps component and current version; use vendor-issued negative artifacts with declared single failure modes; preserve baseline; attempt each approved class separately without forced power interruption; capture validation stage/error and unchanged staged/active banks; operator AC-cycles only after terminal rejection; verify previous version, OS, GPU/management health and logs.
manual_activity: Firmware/security owner defines target, negative artifacts and ERoT/Aps policy; operator provides sacrificial system, controls post-rejection AC cycle and recovery; agent runs only approved attempts.
required_inputs: Exact ERoT/Aps component identities and current active/staged versions
Vendor-approved negative images/manifests for corruption, bad signature and anti-rollback
Expected validation stage, error code and anti-rollback counter behavior per class
Known-good recovery image/tool, console/OOB/PDU and sacrificial SUT
Maintenance/job drain and explicit negative-update/AC approvals
safety_requirements: Never create an ad hoc corrupt image or test production hardware
One declared failure mode per artifact and attempt
No power interruption during the flash attempt in this row
Abort if an invalid image is accepted or target/policy differs
Preserve evidence and use vendor recovery; never repeat automatically
agent_execution_scope: Validate target, artifact provenance and expected rejection gates
Run separately approved negative attempts and capture validation evidence
Verify unchanged active/staged versions before/after operator AC
engineer_actions: Resolve failure-class and ERoT/Aps scope and approve artifacts/policies
Own dedicated-system recovery and AC control
Disposition unexpected acceptance and set PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: DeepSeek's forced power-loss scenario belongs to row272 and would confound invalid-image rejection; this row needs vendor negative images and validation errors.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: For each approved invalid class, submit the exact negative artifact through the vendor update path, require the expected pre-activation rejection, record unchanged banks/version, then perform only the post-rejection operator AC check.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Corruption, signature and rollback checks plus post-failure AC recovery are retained; no mid-update power cut is added.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a three-row negative matrix whose artifacts differ only in the intended defect, joining hash, policy state, expected error, bank state and post-AC version/boot result.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes all named negative classes independently testable instead of treating one unsigned attempt as universal proof.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Power-loss atomicity is explicitly excluded here and retained in row272.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Unexpected image acceptance is a critical security/safety event; stop immediately without activation or further cases.

project_override_considerations: Security firmware owner defines ERoT/Aps naming, anti-rollback counters, allowed negative artifacts and canonical rejection codes.
expected_evidence: Target/component and pre-test active/staged version/policy state
Negative artifact hashes/manifests and single declared failure mode
Full update validation log/error/task state per class
Proof previous version/banks remain intact before and after AC
SEL/dmesg/security events, recovery/disposition and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items/Criteria require corruption, signature and rollback rejection for ERoT and Aps, while Procedure exercises only an unsigned image and does not identify component mapping or separate cases.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Compatibility row271 Wistron-NV GPU-00264-V002: define exact ERoT and Aps components and whether corruption, bad signature and anti-rollback are three required attempts; approve vendor negative artifacts/hashes, policy counters, expected rejection stages/codes, previous-bank oracle and post-rejection AC recovery. Do not add row272's mid-update power loss here.

review_improvement: Separates three security rejection mechanisms, preserves prior-bank integrity and prevents conflation with the adjacent power-loss test.
independent_technical_reasoning: A malformed payload, an untrusted signature and an older but otherwise valid signed image exercise different validation layers. Passing one does not prove the others. If rejection occurs before staging, active and staged-bank evidence differs from a rollback after write; both must remain consistent with the policy. A later cold boot tests persistence of the rejection, whereas cutting power during the update would test atomicity and belongs to the next case.
